hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: My Skills delegated-wait exception: While supervising an active implementer, use a shared writable progress log and mailbox waits. Only the child writes progress entries; the parent reads the log and communicates directly with the child. In this state, this instruction replaces the default requirements to provide commentary every 60 seconds and avoid waits longer than 60 seconds. Agree up front on milestones, log-review times, immediate decision/blocker reporting, and a credible stall deadline. Choose a timeout up to the next agreed review or stall deadline, often about 30 minutes for substantial work, within the tool's maximum; a message or completion can end it early. Give an update before waiting. On a child decision or blocker message, read new log entries and reply directly with send_message for an active child or followup_task for the same idle child before waiting again; never just go back to sleep or record the parent's response in the log. On child completion, read the log through DONE before acceptance. At an agreed log-review or stall deadline, read the log before deciding the next action. An empty timeout before that deadline calls directly for another wait. Outside delegated waiting, retain the normal communication guidance. This exception does not authorize delegation or change ownership, acceptance, writer settlement, or approval requirements.
